paper.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
paper.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

paper.title: Microcausality Bounds on Dispersion Laws
paper.abstract: Microcausality holds in any state, including those that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and requires the poles (and other singularities) of the retarded Green's function to satisfy $\mathrm{Im}\,ω\le |\mathrm{Im}\,k|$ throughout the complex plane. Building on the work of Heller, Serantes, Spaliński and Withers, we study its consequences for dispersion relations that are linear at small $k$, like Goldstone bosons, assuming tree-level, non-dissipative dynamics. We show that microcausality is equivalent to requiring that $k \pm ω(k)$ be typically real functions. This yields two-sided bounds on all higher-order coefficients of $ω(k)$ in units of its radius of convergence $R$, the scale at which the linear Goldstone description breaks down. The optimal constraints are characterised by an infinite hierarchy of Toeplitz determinants. We derive analogous bounds on $ω^2(k)$, whose radius of convergence $\tilde R$ marks the scale at which new states must appear. The bounds shrink to zero as the sound speed $c_s$ approaches 1: for a fixed higher-derivative correction, both $R$ and $\tilde R$ become parametrically smaller than naive dimensional analysis suggests. In particular, in the EFT of Inflation all higher-derivative quadratic operators must vanish as $c_s \to 1$. We test the bounds in several models: a $U(1)$ superfluid, light in a dielectric medium, photon propagation in a strong magnetic field, colour-flavour-locked quark matter, and a homogeneous solid. Finally, we extend the bounds to gapped modes.

paper.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
paper.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

paper.title: Observables and Symmetries in Causal Fermion System
paper.abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.

paper.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
paper.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.

paper.title: Black Hole Superradiance and the Gravitational Auger Effect
paper.abstract: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of nature's light degrees of freedom. In the vicinity of a spinning black hole, it exponentially amplifies ultralight bosons from vacuum fluctuations to a macroscopic cloud of enormous occupation number. Observational superradiance effects - modified black-hole spins, gravitational-wave and coherent boson emission - are known to depend sensitively on bosonic self-interactions as induced by a quartic, $λφ^4$. Here we point out that purely gravitational interactions within the cloud significantly modify superradiance dynamics, through an analog of the Auger effect. Moreover, we identify nontrivial evolution of the superradiant levels beyond the first, driven by scattering into even higher levels and their radial overtones. For the QCD axion, the irreducible gravitational coupling rapidly dissipates the first superradiant level after it reaches saturation, through scalar emission and absorption by the black hole, while truncating the growth of higher levels. This can dramatically suppress the observability of continuous gravitational-wave signals or signatures in late binary inspirals. Black hole spin-down remains more robust, but for higher modes begins earlier and proceeds more slowly, requiring revision of existing limits.

paper.title: Interpreting JWST UV luminosity functions and angular correlation functions via a "universal language" for high-redshift galaxies
paper.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) found more bright $z\gtrsim10$ galaxies than expected before its launch. No consensus has emerged on whether difficulties in reproducing them stem from missing physics, simplifying assumptions that break down at the highest redshifts, or model mis-calibration. This is complicated because most galaxy models cannot be compared like-to-like, and models invoking different physical processes can make similar predictions for compressed summaries such as ultraviolet luminosity functions (UV LFs). Here we describe galaxy populations in a universal language: a chain of physically and empirically motivated conditional distributions linking halo mass, stellar mass, star formation rate and UV magnitude, defined consistently across models and data. We build a broad prior from fits to five hydrodynamic simulations, which predict very different high-redshift galaxy populations. We infer the parameters of this flexible galaxy model from $z>6$ JWST observations of UV LFs and angular correlation functions (ACFs). Including the mass-complete ACFs disfavors a large scatter around the stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR). With simulation-based priors, the star-forming main sequence (SFMS) is described by a star-formation timescale of about one halo dynamical time, and the scatter around the SFMS increases toward lower stellar masses. The SFMS scatter is the main source of stochasticity in UV magnitude at fixed halo mass, accounting for a median $\sim$61% of the variance at $M_{\rm UV}=-20$ (SHMR scatter: $\sim$36%). Bayesian model selection finds no evidence for redshift evolution of the SHMR or for an SFMS slope different from unity. At $z\sim20$, our fiducial model predicts UV LFs orders of magnitude below estimates from photometric candidates. A consensus on the discrepant UV LF estimates at $z\geq14$ is needed to determine whether model extensions are required.

paper.title: Polarized equatorial emission around regular compact objects
paper.abstract: We study the polarization properties of regular compact objects motivated by quantum gravity. These geometries include static spherically symmetric non-singular black holes which undergo a continuous transition to regular particle-like spacetimes in certain regions of the parametric space. Applying a phenomenological model of a magnetized fluid ring orbiting in the equatorial plane, we search for characteristic signatures in the direct polarized images which could distinguish them from black holes in general relativity. At low inclinations the regular compact objects lead to a very similar polarization pattern as the Schwarzschild black hole. At high inclinations we observe a characteristic signature for the particle-like geometries. A second direct image of the fluid ring is formed which is absent for black holes. It may possess with three orders of magnitude higher polarization intensity and a specific polarization direction making it observationally significant. We elucidate the physical mechanism for the formation of the second direct image and pinpoint the plasma configurations which lead to amplification of its polarized emission.

paper.title: Searching for Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence with SPT-3G
paper.abstract: We search for anisotropic cosmic birefringence using two years of data from the SPT-3G instrument on the South Pole Telescope. Anisotropic cosmic birefringence refers to a theorized dependence of the refractive index of the vacuum on the polarization of light that varies across the Universe in a statistically isotropic manner. Such an effect would manifest as a direction-dependent mixing of the $E$ and $B$ polarization modes of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), caused by rotation of the polarization angle as photons travel from the CMB last scattering surface to us. We present a measurement of the power spectrum of the rotation angle $α$ in six bins across the angular multipole range $20 < L < 2048$, finding no evidence for cosmic birefringence with the spectrum consistent with zero. At 95% confidence, we set a new best upper limit on the amplitude of a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum of $A_{\rm CB}<0.027$. Additionally, we place upper limits on a scale-dependent white noise model. We translate the scale-invariant upper limit to constraints on the axion coupling constant and primordial magnetic field strength, finding 95% confidence limits of $g_{αγ} < 1.7\times 10^{-2}/H_I$ and $B_{\rm 1\,Mpc} < 9.6\,{\rm nG}$ respectively. We expect these limits to improve several-fold with the complete SPT-3G survey.

paper.title: Landauer erasure and horizon information in an expanding universe
paper.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic cost of information erasure in Friedmann--Robertson--Walker cosmology by combining Landauer's principle with the thermodynamics of the apparent horizon. Adopting the apparent-horizon temperature as an effective cosmological temperature, we find that for standard non-phantom expansion, the minimum heat required to erase one bit decreases while the entropy-equivalent information content of the horizon increases. We further compare the Landauer heat with the Misner--Sharp energy and show that, despite their simple thermodynamic relation, they have distinct physical meanings. These results provide a simple connection between information erasure, horizon thermodynamics, and gravitational energy in an expanding universe.

paper.title: On the Prospects of Using Cyclic Spectroscopy on Canonical Pulsars
paper.abstract: We use the cyclic figure of merit to determine the likelihood of achieving cyclic deconvolution for 2609 canonical pulsars, a population for which this technique has not previously been used. These pulsars have spin periods between 0.1 and 10 seconds and are surveyed across 15 different telescope-observing frequency combinations. We conclude that cyclic deconvolution will only be a viable method for pulse broadening function or phase retrieval recovery in a handful of canonical pulsars. Few, if any, pulsars pass the conservative threshold for a given telescope-frequency combination. We believe that the cyclic figure of merit does not accurately reflect our ability to use cyclic deconvolution on this population, instead showing a shortcoming of the measurement when observing canonicals at low observing frequencies. Still, it is reliable for MSPs and for canonicals at high observing frequencies. More promising is the prospect of using this technique to recover scintles for canonical pulsars; DSA and FAST are best-suited for this as judged by the number of sources where scintles may be resolved and S/N is sufficient. We suspect there may be more sources that would have large figures of cyclic merit, but insufficient S/N, at very low frequencies. We advocate for expansions of real-time cyclic spectroscopy backends for current and upcoming low frequency telescopes.

paper.title: Primordial Non-Gaussianity and Correlation-Function Perturbativity in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
paper.abstract: We investigate primordial non-Gaussianity and the perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We construct the cubic interaction Hamiltonian in the canonical representation of the quadratic theory and derive an exact finite-momentum in-in expression for the tree-level bispectrum. We consider two initial-state prescriptions: a Gaussian state specified at the bounce and the de Sitter vacuum specified at a remote contracting surface. We assess the retained nonlinear-conversion correction through $Ξ=|ΔP_R/P_R^{(0)}|$. For the bounce state, a conservative, cancellation-independent, finite-window absolute-integrand estimate is below $6\times10^{-6}$ at all five sampled momenta. For the remote de Sitter state, the signed correction is dominated by cancellations and decreases from $Ξ\simeq9.9\times10^{-2}$ at one tenth of the bounce-curvature scale to $Ξ\simeq2.3\times10^{-4}$ at that scale. Although the retained two-point corrections remain below unity, the bispectrum can have large pointwise amplitudes: the bounce state yields an equilateral $f_{\rm NL}$ with root-mean-square amplitude over oscillation phase of order $10^3$--$10^4$, while the remote state can yield much larger values. The dominant rapid oscillation is organized approximately by $k_t=k_1+k_2+k_3$, with $Δk_t\simeq5.7\times10^{-4}m_{\rm P}$, while the triangle-shape envelope varies slowly. For the illustrative bounce-to-present mapping adopted here, CMB-projection diagnostics indicate substantial phase averaging. Thus, large pointwise primordial non-Gaussianity can coexist with a small retained correction to the two-point function.

paper.title: Asymptotic stability of axisymmetric perturbations of near-horizon extremal Kerr with a Schwarzian-deformed throat
paper.abstract: We study the asymptotic stability of axisymmetric gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometries of (near-)extremal Kerr black holes and consider the family of backgrounds in which the AdS$_{2}$ factor of NHEK is deformed by a Schwarzian mode. Requiring the Killing parameter to be local in the background makes the Gelfand--Dikii polynomials natural solutions of the Killing equation, and that locality requirement brings stationary solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation. The hierarchy selects a family of backgrounds, which remain $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\times \mathfrak{u}(1)$ throughout them: the first level gives NHEK and near-NHEK, the second, solitons that depart from one of these geometries and return to it. We linearize Einstein's equations around this family, where the axisymmetric sector reduces to a wave equation on the nearly-AdS$_{2}$ base, and analyze this equation by energy and virial methods. For NHEK we obtain a conserved energy, an integrated local energy estimate and asymptotic stability in a weighted norm; for a nonconstant Schwarzian the energy becomes a Lyapunov functional whose monotonicity is dictated by the sign of its derivative, yielding uniform bounds for integrable ones, and mild local decay along the KdV soliton. We also find a monotone horizon-localized norm, which is not of Aretakis type, showing that stability properties are directly sensitive to the near-horizon structure encoded in the Schwarzian background. We compute the associated Regge--Teitelboim charges at a late-time corner of the throat using a radial ADM foliation of the spacetime.

paper.title: Quantifying the Dominance and Emergence of Brightest Cluster Galaxies in SPT and Planck Clusters: A Novel Application of the Gini Index
paper.abstract: We introduce the Gini index (G) as a metric for studying the emergence of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) by quantifying the disparity in the light distribution of galaxy cluster cores. The Gini index collapses the skewness of the bright-end luminosity function to a single statistic, and provides a measure for the light dominance of the BCG over other cluster members that is more robust than the magnitude gap. We argue that the Gini index is far less sensitive to short-term changes in the cluster dynamical state than the magnitude gap and solves its known degeneracies by taking the entire cluster membership into account, making G a more sensitive metric to long-term BCG assembly. We apply the magnitude gap and Gini index to a progenitor-selected sample of 92 South Pole Telescope- and Planck-selected cluster cores at 0 < z < 1 with corresponding Hubble Space Telescope F110W and F200LP and Sloan Digital Sky Survey g and r photometry. Based on both parametric and empirical tests, we find no statistical evidence for evolution in G or $\rm M_{1,2}$ over 0 < z < 1, and find that BCGs have not grown significantly (2${\times}$) faster than the cluster population for z < 1 at 3$σ$ confidence. This implies that BCGs achieve dominance and establish defining properties early (z > 1) in massive clusters. In general, we find that the Gini index is a valuable and relatively straightforward measurement, with well-controlled systematics, that could be applied to much larger samples to study BCG dominance and emergence.

paper.title: 3D Radiative Transfer Simulations for Characterization of the Optically Thick DART Ejecta Plume
paper.abstract: The Hyperion package is a three-dimensional Monte-Carlo radiative transfer approach to modeling dust ejecta. Because it has proven to be a powerful tool for simulating optically thick environments with complicated structure, we are applying the routines to observations of the DART impact on asteroid Dimorphos. Our analysis focuses on the LICIACube LUKE red-filter image acquired 175 s after impact, when the near-surface plume remained dense and not strongly structured. The model incorporates the updated Dimorphos shape model, spacecraft and solar geometry derived, and size-dependent scattering properties of realistic dust particles. We adopt an axisymmetric conical ejecta geometry and iteratively adjust the particle size distribution (PSD) and vertical number density profile to reproduce observed brightness profiles extracted from the LUKE image. We find that a power-law PSD with slope k = 3.0 and a number density peak located at approximately 120 m above the surface best reproduces the brightness contrast between the illuminated surface, the bright ejecta plume, and the adjacent dark band produced by shadowing within the optically thick material. The resulting best-fit model implies a total ejecta mass of 1.25 x 10^6 kg within 500 m of the impact site.

paper.title: High-Resolution DKIST/ViSP Observation Reveals Small-scale Photospheric Magnetic Flux beneath a Coronal Hole Region
paper.abstract: The magnetic unipolarity of photospheric regions beneath coronal holes is well established at spatial resolutions of about 1 arcsecond, but the effect of smaller-scale magnetic structures remains uncertain. We compare co-aligned observations from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the Visible Spectro-Polarimeter (ViSP) at the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST). HMI observes the Fe I 6173 Å line, while ViSP observes the Fe I 6302.5 Å line; both form at similar photospheric heights. We derive the line-of-sight magnetic field (B_LOS) from ViSP spectropolarimetric data using a Milne-Eddington inversion and compare it with the HMI field derived from vector magnetograms over a common coronal-hole region. ViSP detects smaller magnetic structures with stronger fields than HMI. The absolute mean field and mean absolute field are higher by factors of 1.30 and 1.37, respectively. HMI measures approximately 28% less unsigned magnetic flux and 24% less net signed magnetic flux than ViSP. A comparison of spatially degraded ViSP data with HMI indicates that differences in effective resolution and associated spatial averaging contribute to these discrepancies. Nevertheless, the magnetic flux imbalance remains similar: 69% for HMI and 65% for ViSP. Thus, the additional small-scale flux detected by ViSP does not substantially change the measured unipolarity in this region. Because ViSP has a limited field of view, observations covering entire coronal holes are needed to test whether this result holds more generally.

paper.title: Cosmography with gravitational waves II: Padé approximants in an extended redshift regime
paper.abstract: We evaluate the capability of next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, including LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and DECIGO, to probe cosmographic parameters using electromagnetically bright standard sirens. Adopting Padé approximants, we extend the cosmographic analysis to substantially higher redshifts and constrain the parameters $H_0$, $q_0$, $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$. We examine the constraints primarily as a function of the number of detections and, in a complementary analysis, across correlated SNR--redshift regimes. LISA provides percent-level constraints on $H_0$, while the Einstein Telescope and DECIGO reach subpercent precision as the catalogue size increases. The parameter $q_0$ can be constrained at the tens-of-percent level, whereas the higher-order parameters $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$ remain progressively less determined. Compared with the low-redshift Taylor analysis, the Padé approach extends the usable redshift range, increases the accessible event population and enables a higher-order reconstruction of the expansion history.

paper.title: Comets in Kepler background photometry: the ion tail and tail disconnection of C/2009 K5 (McNaught) and an analysis of comets crossing the Kepler field
paper.abstract: Kepler recorded several thousand dedicated sky-background pixels per detector output every 29.4 min from 2009 to 2013, an archive that we use to study comets. During 2010 April 14-21 a narrow band of excess light swept across the field at 1.46 deg/day. This feature is the ion tail of comet C/2009 K5 (McNaught), whose head passed just beyond the edge of the detector array. We trace the tail from 0.9 deg to ~13 deg from the nucleus at surface brightnesses of 26.7-30 mag/arcsec^2; its aberration implies a solar-wind speed of ~500-750 km/s. At 30-min cadence we follow a tail-disconnection event on 2010 April 17-19 whose timing and geometry are consistent with a flank encounter with a coronal mass ejection, although other triggers cannot be excluded. We then analyze all 21 known comets with perihelion distance q < 15 AU whose heads crossed the detectors, using photometry at the predicted head positions calibrated against displaced control tracks. Eight comets are detected, including C/2010 J4 (WISE) a few days before its discovery and two comets at 6.3-7.4 AU with one-sided streaks that we interpret as dust tails. The undetected comets give 3-sigma limits of typically Kp > 16.6-18.1 within 5 arcmin of the head. A blind shift-and-stack search for moving diffuse sources, roughly 50% complete at Kp ~ 15.5-16 for rates of 0.3-1 deg/day, recovers four known comets and finds no unknown ones. Animations show the K5 tail and comets C/2011 L3 and C/2010 J4 crossing the field.

paper.title: The Stability Frontier of Interacting Binary Stars
paper.abstract: We derive a conservation based dynamical stability frontier for interacting binary stars that distinguishes stationary mass transfer from the restoration of a perturbed contact state. We apply the formalism to conservative white dwarf binaries with direct impact accretion, coupling Roche overflow, stream angular momentum, gravitational radiation, and both stellar spin reservoirs. From the contact equations, we obtain the required orbital return torque, and an exact Jacobian identity yields the restoring gradient and an oscillatory stability boundary in the computed white dwarf domain. A dimensionally normalized quadrupolar tide reveals separate equilibrium fold and oscillatory thresholds, including coexisting stable and unstable stationary branches. Finite donor synchronization introduces an additional oscillatory stability frontier. The model recovers the classical Roche and gravitational radiation limits, while the calculated orbital period derivatives are consistent with published binary timing measurements within their combined observational and model uncertainties. These results specify the torque amplitude, restoring stiffness, and synchronization rate needed for local stability, providing quantitative targets for stellar tidal calculations and the interpretation of interacting binaries in the millihertz gravitational wave band.

paper.title: Early Spectroscopy of the Type II SN 2024phv Suggests Short-Lived Circumstellar Interaction
paper.abstract: We present the high-cadence light curve and rapid spectroscopy of the Type II SN 2024phv, discovered just 16.8 hours after the estimated explosion time. The early light curve exhibits a rapid 2 mag rise over the first day of observation, and spectra at 1.7 and 2.6 days reveal weak, narrow emission lines, suggesting moderate interaction with circumstellar material during the first few days after explosion. Models of shock-cooling emission provide a reasonable fit to the light curve after day 2, implying minimal interaction at later epochs, and yield a best-fit progenitor radius of $R=390\pm90\,R_{\odot}$. We also compare our earliest spectra with radiation hydrodynamical models of exploding red supergiants to measure circumstellar densities of ${\sim}10^{-12}$ g cm$^{-3}$ within a few stellar radii of the progenitor, followed by a sharp dropoff in the density profile. This rapidly decreasing profile leads us to conclude that the progenitor of SN 2024phv had an extended atmosphere and/or closely confined circumstellar material, likely from rapidly increasing or eruptive mass loss prior to explosion. In the context of other supernovae discovered at similarly early phases, SN 2024phv points to a diversity in the mass-loss rates of red supergiant stars in their final years.

paper.title: A Bound on Wormhole Probing Time from Holographic Multi-Entropy
paper.abstract: Bipartite entanglement entropy eventually saturates and therefore cannot track the continued growth of an eternal wormhole. Recently, it was shown that genuine tripartite multi-entropy can probe wormhole growth even after bipartite entanglement entropies have saturated. This naturally raises the question: can increasing the number of parties extend the probing time indefinitely? Adopting the multiway maximin prescription and assuming that its selected representatives are regular spacetime-stationary networks, we prove that the answer is no for nonrotating BTZ black holes. We establish a common finite upper bound on the probing time for every fixed finite boundary partition, independent of the number, sizes, and arrangement of its parties. For any network on any Cauchy slice, there exists a comparison network that assigns the entire central region containing the wormhole interior to a single party. A network longer than this comparison network cannot minimize length on that slice. The central length required by a stationary network connecting the two boundaries grows with time, whereas the central length of the comparison network remains uniformly bounded. At sufficiently late times, such a network therefore cannot minimize length on any Cauchy slice containing it and is excluded from the maximin prescription. Consequently, beyond this bound, no network selected by maximin enters the black-hole interior.

paper.title: Nearby M&M Binaries Uncovered with the Gaia Multipeak Fraction and Speckle Interferometry
paper.abstract: Multipeak fraction is a strong indicator of stellar multiplicity with subarcsecond angular separation in the Gaia DR3 catalog. We select 18 sources with multipeak fraction above 5% among stars possibly in the 20 pc solar neighborhood with as yet unconfirmed binarity. We successfully resolve eleven systems of M-type dwarf components in speckle interferometric observations with a 2.5 m telescope at the Caucasian Mountain Observatory of Sternberg Astronomical Institute, Moscow State University. The tentatively estimated companion masses lie in the 0.09 -- 0.23 $M_\odot$ range. All six sources with a multipeak fraction of 6--8% are unresolved, suggesting an observational bias that affects nearby stars.

paper.title: Projected DKP spin-1 sectors in a $(2+1)$-dimensional static wormhole: Self-duality, helicity content, and spectral correspondence
paper.abstract: We use the projected spin-1 Duffin--Kemmer--Petiau (DKP) equation in $2+1$ dimensions to clarify the physical content of the irreducible $3\times3$ representations. The projected antisymmetric tensor is algebraically dual to the projected vector, and the two twin representations select conjugate self-dual covariant-curl sectors, which reduce to opposite massive helicities in the flat-space limit. We then apply this structure to the static wormhole problem previously studied with a single irreducible representation. The first-order radial DKP system contains an exceptional normalizable bound-state branch at $ω^2=M^2$ that is absent from the master-variable reduction, whereas the generic master and circular sectors are related by a Darboux transformation. The latter preserves the transmission and reflection probabilities, while the quasinormal modes are organized into two pole families in the complex radial-momentum plane, leading to the physical pairing $(ω,-ω^*)$ rather than a global $\pmω$ prescription.

paper.title: The fate of hidden symmetries under magnetic Harrison transformations
paper.abstract: Solution-generating transformations construct new geometries from known seeds, raising the question of whether and to what extent the resulting solutions inherit the hidden symmetries underlying the seeds' integrability and separability. We have established universal perturbative inheritance laws for CKTs and massless scalar separability directly at the level of magnetic Harrison transformations, encompassing both magnetization of Carter-type seeds and demagnetization of conformal Carter-type seeds. In both magnetized Kerr and demagnetized Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson, this perturbative inheritance coexists with the loss of exact Carter-type separability, while seed-connected conformal Killing-Yano structures are already obstructed at the same perturbative order. These results reveal a hierarchy in the perturbative survival of hidden symmetries and provide a framework for investigating their inheritance in more general theoretical settings and under other solution-generating transformations.

paper.title: ASASSN-15af: An Eclipsing Cataclysmic Variable above the Period Gap Showing Both Positive and Negative Superhump-like Signals
paper.abstract: We present a photometric study of ASASSN-15af (TIC~231050794), combining TESS full-frame-image photometry from the TEQUILA project with 2-minute SPOC light curves and archival ASAS-SN and ATLAS monitoring over 4400~d. The long-term light curve shows recurrent dwarf-nova outbursts, establishing ASASSN-15af as a high-inclination eclipsing dwarf nova above the canonical period gap. From 391 quiescent eclipses, we derive the working ephemeris $T(E)=2139.76108(3)+0.14982063(2)\,E$ (BTJD), corresponding to $P_{\rm orb}=3.596$~hr. A quadratic fit is formally better, but the timings sample only three widely separated epochs, so we regard the apparent O--C curvature as tentative. In quiescence, the out-of-eclipse waveform is dominated by a stable $2f_{\rm orb}$ component, consistent with a substantial ellipsoidal contribution from the donor; during the Sector~96 outburst, its fractional amplitude decreases by $\simeq66\%$, consistent with dilution by the brightened disk. The outburst-only signals occur at periods $\sim1.6\%$ shorter than $P_{\rm orb}$ in Sector~2 and $\sim3.1\%$ longer in Sector~96, consistent with negative- and positive-superhump-like modulations, respectively. Because each is detected in only one outburst, their recurrence remains to be established. Their period-offset ratio, $φ\simeq0.51$, is consistent with empirical trends among systems showing both modes, while the inferred superhump-based mass ratios span $q\simeq0.06$--$0.24$. During the Sector~96 outburst, the eclipse deepens by $ΔD=0.196\pm0.028$ and its centroid shifts earlier by $Δt_{\rm c}=-66.6\pm7.3$~s, indicating a redistribution of accretion-powered light. These results identify ASASSN-15af as an above-gap eclipsing dwarf nova with a dynamically variable accretion disk; spectroscopy is needed to constrain the mass ratio.

paper.title: Drift of a Charged Particle in a Black Hole Magnetosphere: the Effect of Black Hole Spin
paper.abstract: Sparse plasma immersed in a strong magnetic field is common in astrophysical scenarios, for which a collisionless description is more appropriate. The guiding-center approximation serves as an effective tool for describing the motion of charged particles in a strong magnetic field, revealing the drift, a sub-leading order motion that causes particles to deviate from the magnetic field lines. It is widely accepted that the charged particles drift under the induction of gravity in Newtonian framework. However, a covariant formulation of the guiding-center approximation, as well as the drift of a charged particle induced by strong gravitational field, has yet to be fully explored. As a preliminary study, we aim to analyze the drift of a single charged particle in a black hole magnetosphere via a covariant approach. Particularly, we focus on the effects of black hole spin. We first examine the drift caused by the rotation of a massive object in the Newtonian regime using the language of gravitoelectromagnetism. A covariant formula of drift is derived, which is confirmed to reduce to the Newtonian results in the weak gravitational field and low speed limit. The impact of BH spin on the drift is analyzed in detail in Kerr spacetime specifically, for which we define the drift rate whose value quantifies the significance of the drift. Our results indicate that the impact of BH spin on the drift of a charged particle in a BH magnetosphere can be comparable to that of other factors in some extreme cases.

paper.title: Testing General Relativity by Reconstructing Dark Energy and the Growth Index with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
paper.abstract: We extend the Cosmo-PINN, a physics-informed neural network for model-independent cosmological reconstruction, to reconstruct the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ and the growth index $γ(z)$ of matter perturbations. The reconstruction is performed through three modules: the background module, the matter growth module, and the growth index module. The background module learns the dark energy density $ρ_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ from cosmological observations, and $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ is reconstructed through the residual of the conservation equation. The reconstructed background is then passed to the other two modules, which reconstruct the observables $f(z)$ and $fσ_{8}(z)$ either directly from the linear perturbation equation of General Relativity or through an independently reconstructed growth index $γ(z)$. Comparing the two reconstructions on the same background provides a consistency test of the underlying physical framework. The network is trained on the DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernovae, and redshift-space distortion data. Posterior uncertainties for the reconstructed cosmological parameters and functions are obtained through Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling. For the different data combinations, the posterior median of the present-day dark energy equation of state lies within the range $w_{\mathrm{DE,0}}\in \lbrack -0.930,-0.867]$, while the phantom divide crossing takes place at $z\simeq 0.41$--$0.53$. The posterior median of the present-day growth index reconstructed from the data lies within $γ_{0}\simeq 0.60$--$0.62$, indicating suppression of the growth of cosmic structure.

paper.title: OGLE-2018-BLG-0829L: A Microlensing System with a Planet Orbiting a Star Possessing a Brown-Dwarf Companion
paper.abstract: We analyze the microlensing event OGLE-2018-BLG-0829, whose light curve exhibits a weak short-term anomaly in addition to the prominent caustic-crossing features of a binary lens. The anomaly cannot be explained by a binary-lens single-source (2L1S) model. We therefore investigate both binary-lens binary-source (2L2S) and triple-lens single-source (3L1S) interpretations and find that both models reproduce the additional anomaly, with the 3L1S model being favored by $Δχ^2=15.1$. Under the favored 3L1S interpretation, the anomaly arises from a caustic induced by a planetary-mass companion, whereas the prominent caustic-crossing features are produced by the underlying binary lens. Combining the measured event timescale, $t_{\rm E}=7.55\pm0.30$ days, and angular Einstein radius, $θ_{\rm E}=0.325 \pm 0.059$ mas, with a Bayesian analysis, we infer a lens system consisting of an M dwarf of mass $0.193^{+0.300}_{-0.098}\,M_\odot$, a possible brown-dwarf companion of mass $0.068^{+0.105}_{-0.034}\,M_\odot$, and a Saturn-mass planet of mass $0.337^{+0.522}_{-0.171}\,M_{\rm J}$. The companions have projected separations of approximately 3.6 au and 1.6 au from the primary, respectively. However, the physical interpretation remains tentative because potentially important higher-order effects have not been considered, and the dynamical stability of the proposed configuration remains uncertain. If confirmed, this would be the third star--brown dwarf--planet system identified through microlensing, highlighting the potential of microlensing to detect planets in complex multiple systems.

paper.abstract: We study spin-induced chaos around a static, spherically symmetric black hole in revised Deser--Woodard nonlocal gravity (NLG), using the conservative test-body approximation relevant to extreme-mass-ratio inspirals. The deformation parameter $ζ$ describes departures from Schwarzschild spacetime. Poincaré sections, rotation curves, and fast Lyapunov indicators (FLIs) reveal changes in resonant structures and a decreasing fraction of non-plunging trajectories classified as chaotic within the sampled family, from $37.5\%$ at $ζ=0$ to zero at $ζ=0.1$. The FLI classifications of selected trajectories are reflected in their approximate mass-quadrupole waveforms: neighboring chaotic and regular trajectories show a marked local spectral-flatness contrast, which weakens in backgrounds where both are classified as regular. To assess whether a transition from chaotic to regular motion caused by the background deformation helps distinguish NLG from GR, we compare NLG waveforms at $ζ=10^{-6}$ with GR waveforms generated at different initial radii. For a trajectory whose classification changes between the backgrounds, this adjustment substantially reduces the mismatch. The selected NLG waveforms from chaotic orbits retain larger minimum mismatches than those from regular orbits, although sensitivity to initial conditions may also hinder signal recovery. These results connect background-dependent orbital dynamics with radiation spectra, but do not establish that chaos offers an advantage for identifying the background geometry.

paper.title: Numerical evidence for the validity of the inverse hoop conjecture for black holes
paper.abstract: The inverse hoop (IH) conjecture, ${\cal M}_{\text{irr}}\leq {\cal C}_{\text{s}}/4π$, originally discussed in the context of stationary black-hole configurations, suggests that the surface area of a black hole cannot undergo unconstrained geometric wrinkling (here ${\cal M}_{\text{irr}}=\sqrt{{\cal A}/16π}$ is the irreducible mass associated with the horizon area ${\cal A}$ of the black hole and ${\cal C}_{\text{s}}$ is the circumference length of the smallest ring that can engulf the horizon of the black hole in every direction). In the present compact paper we provide evidence supporting the validity of the IH conjecture for non-stationary black-hole configurations. In particular, we show that all the non-stationary black-hole solutions recently constructed by Croft, García-Moreno, and Pani (CGP) [arXiv:2611.13266] satisfy the IH relation.

paper.title: Bayesian Time-Varying Spectral Estimation for LISA with P-Splines
paper.abstract: We model the evolutionary spectrum of a slowly time-varying process by a linear combination of products of time- and frequency-dependent B-splines, placing a Gaussian tensor-product penalty prior on the coefficients. The posterior distribution is obtained by updating the prior using a Whittle-type likelihood approximation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency coefficients. Separate regularisation in time and frequency allows non-stationary spectral structure to be inferred. An adaptive coarse-grained likelihood reduces the computational cost while preserving fine resolution around sharp spectral features. We first validate the method using repeated simulations of a locally stationary process with known spectrum, showing lower reconstruction errors and narrower posterior intervals as the sample size increases. We then apply it to a year-long simulated LISA data set with stationary instrumental single link spectra, an evolving time-delay interferometry (TDI) response, and a modulated Galactic foreground. We compare a flexible total power spectral density (PSD) model with models incorporating progressively stronger physical information and examine both continuous and gapped observations. Allowing time variation substantially improves reconstruction relative to a stationary model, while incorporating physical information about the TDI response further improves recovery, particularly near its moving spectral features. The results illustrate the trade-off between spectral flexibility, physical assumptions, and posterior uncertainty in non-stationary LISA noise estimation.

paper.title: Initial Conditions Dictate Gas-Stellar Counter-Rotation in Galaxies
paper.abstract: We present a physical origin of gas-stellar counter-rotation in galaxies. Scale-dependent partitions of tidal torques from cosmic primordial perturbations source angular momentum for distinct baryonic components. This scale dependence maps to radial hierarchy in Lagrangian space clustering: stellar components, assembled at earlier times from the inner protohalo, retain persistent memory of small-scale tidal torques, whereas gas, accreted later from outer Lagrangian regions, is governed by large-scale perturbations and can develop counter-rotation. This mechanism is observationally testable and offers a direct probe of the hierarchical cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm. Unlike conventional late-time scenarios that only explain the existence of counter-rotation, our framework further predicts its component-resolved direction, enabling component-resolved angular momentum to serve as a new probe of primordial density perturbations and improving cosmological initial condition reconstruction.

paper.title: Holographic Entanglement after a Global Quench in Noncommutative Yang-Mills Theory
paper.abstract: The time evolution of holographic entanglement entropy and mixed-state correlations following a global quench in four-dimensional N=4 noncommutative Yang-Mills theory is investigated using a Vaidya geometry. For strip-shaped regions extended along a noncommutative direction, two distinct early-time growth regimes emerge, depending on the relation between the shell-crossing and noncommutative scales: logarithmic growth, with a coefficient proportional to the injected energy density and the square of the noncommutative scale, followed by quadratic growth. For sufficiently wide strips, an intermediate linear-growth regime appears, governed by an entanglement velocity that increases with noncommutativity. The approach to equilibrium is also examined, revealing the role of the butterfly velocity in the continuous evolution of extremal surfaces, while competing branches can modify the physical saturation time. For two disjoint strips, the leading width-independent logarithmic contribution cancels in the mutual information, whereas the entanglement wedge cross section exhibits an intermediate linear-growth regime governed by the same entanglement velocity, provided the connected entanglement wedge remains dominant.

paper.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
paper.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipostσ$ and lies $\vnsplanckpostσ$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

paper.title: Unveiling Hidden X-ray Broad Line Region in Centaurus A: Broadband Analysis with XRISM and NuSTAR
paper.abstract: We present a broadband X-ray spectral analysis of the radio galaxy Centaurus~A, utilizing simultaneous \textit{XRISM} (Resolve and Xtend) and \textit{NuSTAR} observations. Unlike the previous phenomenological analysis of the Fe K$α$ line (Bogensberger et al. 2025), we employ physical reflection models developed with the radiative transfer code SKIRT. They self-consistently predict the continuum and fluorescent lines from a clumpy torus and an X-ray broad line region (xBLR). The Fe K$α$ complex is well reproduced with a three velocity component model. We interpret this as two narrow torus components (FWHM $= 310\pm50$ and $1900\pm400$~km~s$^{-1}$) and an xBLR component (FWHM $= 6000_{-800}^{+1100}$~km~s$^{-1}$). The inner torus radius of 0.13~pc is 10 times the dust sublimation radius (0.013~pc), implying that the torus in a low-luminosity AGN is not determined by dust-related physics. The xBLR has a substantial covering factor of 0.11--0.36, a hydrogen column density ($5 \times 10^{23}$~cm$^{-2}$), a radius of 0.014~pc from the SMBH, and a mass of $>0.9 M_\odot$. Its mass supply rate is comparable to the accretion rate inferred from the bolometric luminosity, implying efficient xBLR formation even at low Eddington ratios. The xBLR line width also provides a novel estimate of the black-hole mass, $\log{(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot})} = 7.00\pm0.34$, via the optical BLR mass-scaling relation to the Fe~K$α$. This agrees with dynamical measurements within a factor of $\sim5$, consistent with the scatter of the optical relation. We also infer the abundance ratios of $A_{\rm Ca}/A_{\rm Fe} = 1.1_{-0.1}^{+0.2}$ and $A_{\rm Ni}/A_{\rm Fe} = 1.4_{-0.2}^{+0.1}$ solar.

paper.title: Two-scale system: compactified ambient metrics and Scri/Spi/Ti
paper.abstract: We show that certain geometric constructions, including the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric, Brinkmann spaces, and ultrastatic vacuum spacetimes, admit natural conformal compactifications and can be unified within a single framework arising naturally from conformal geometry. The framework is based on a two-scale system comprising two weight-one conformal scalars satisfying almost-Einstein equations and certain regularity conditions. As a particular instance of this unifying framework, we obtain a new ambient construction for Spi and Ti, the extended spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. A remarkable feature of this construction is that Spi/Ti and the null infinity of the corresponding spacetimes are naturally realised as a boundary face and the corner of the two-scale ambient space, respectively. We also demonstrate how the two-scale system can serve as a background ambient geometry for studying the asymptotic behaviour of (gauge) fields at spatial, temporal, and null infinity.

paper.title: Neural Surrogates for Tabulated Nuclear Equations of State in Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations
paper.abstract: Large-scale core-collapse supernova simulations rely on tabulated nuclear equations of state (EOSs), whose memory requirements can become a practical constraint in massively parallel calculations. We explore a compact alternative by replacing the tabulated thermodynamic mapping with a neural-network surrogate, using the Lattimer--Swesty EOS as a representative reference model. The surrogate directly predicts pressure, sound speed, and effective adiabatic index from $(\log ρ, \log e, Y_e)$ and accurately reconstructs the nonlinear thermodynamic structure of the EOS, including its behavior across phase-transition regions. It reproduces one-dimensional shock-tube solutions with hydrodynamic errors at the $\sim 10^{-3}$ level under different thermodynamic conditions and yields hydrostatic equilibrium configurations closely matching those obtained with the reference EOS. We find that smaller regression errors do not necessarily yield better hydrodynamic performance, demonstrating the importance of hydrodynamic validation in surrogate model selection. A compact network with only $\sim 10^4$ parameters retains this accuracy while reducing the memory required to store the EOS from $\sim 160$ MB to $\sim 100$ KB, corresponding to a reduction by a factor of $\sim 1500$. The surrogate also remains stable through collapse, bounce, shock formation, and post-bounce evolution in a one-dimensional adiabatic core-collapse calculation. These results demonstrate the potential of compact neural EOS surrogates for reducing memory requirements in large-scale core-collapse supernova simulations.

paper.title: A Stable Vector Bounce
paper.abstract: We construct a geodesically complete bounce in cubic generalised Proca theory with a free canonical scalar as the matter field. The temporal vector evolves along its algebraic constraint and supports the transition from contraction to expansion while matter obeys the null energy condition. This evolution permits nonzero derivative mixing at the bounce. The kinetic coefficients are positive at every finite time for all nonzero comoving wavenumbers, and short-wavelength perturbations are stable throughout the solution. paper.title: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
paper.abstract: The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. In the $Λ$CDM+$\sum m_ν$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_ν<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino mass. When the model is extended to $w_0w_a$CDM+$\sum m_ν$, both the observed and mock samples yield upper limits of approximately $0.3$--$0.4\,\mathrm{eV}$, indicating that the assumed dark-energy model remains a dominant factor in these constraints. As localized FRB samples grow and the modeling of the individual DM contributions becomes more accurate, FRBs may provide further independent low-redshift information for constraining neutrino mass.

paper.title: Radial Evolution of a Corotating Interaction Region from a High-Resolution MHD Simulation
paper.abstract: Corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are large-scale structures formed by fast--slow solar wind interaction, playing a crucial role in heliospheric dynamics and space weather. However, the evolution of individual CIRs and their full three-dimensional morphology remain poorly understood. We investigate the radial evolution of a single CIR using a high-resolution simulation combined with a backmapping method. The simulation reproduces the major plasma and magnetic signatures observed by Wind at 1~AU and by MAVEN and Tianwen-1 at $\sim$1.6~AU. The CIR exhibits a warped, shell-like spiral structure tilted relative to the heliospheric current sheet, consistent with theoretical predictions. During its developing stage, geometric changes are modest, and the radial scalings of velocity ($V_r \propto r^{0.02}$), density ($N \propto r^{-2.00}$), magnetic field ($B_{\rm total} \propto r^{-1.74}$), and temperature ($T \propto r^{-0.97}$) are comparable to those of the background solar wind. In the mature stage, the CIR drifts in longitude and expands toward high latitudes, while its longitudinal and latitudinal widths decrease with distance. The full-domain scalings change markedly to $V_r \propto r^{0.13}$, $N \propto r^{-1.91}$, $B_{\rm total} \propto r^{0.35}$, and $T \propto r^{-0.52}$, differing from both the background wind and the ecliptic-plane CIR. This study quantifies the radial evolution of a CIR from formation to maturity and highlights the importance of its three-dimensional structure in characterizing its morphology and dynamics.

paper.title: Unbound matter in the circum-halo medium: a common mediator of halo secondary bias
paper.abstract: Halo secondary bias describes the dependence of halo clustering on properties beyond mass. Here we report that a new environmental metric, the unbound matter fraction ($f_{\rm un}$) in the $2$--$3\,R_{\rm vir}$ shell around a halo, can largely account for secondary bias. Using haloes with $M_{\rm vir}=10^{10.5}$--$10^{14.5}h^{-1}{\rm M_\odot}$ at $z=0$ obtained from TNG300-1-Dark, we find that controlling for $f_{\rm un}$ reduces the secondary bias of formation time, concentration, spin, shape and velocity anisotropy to a residual correlation of $\lesssim 4\%$, outperforming other environmental metrics such as the tidal anisotropy for spin and velocity anisotropy. Applying a stacking method to the circum-halo medium (CHM), we identify two distinct flow patterns: low-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes co-move with coherent flows, with the CHM converging onto the haloes; in contrast, high-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes move through dynamically hot, partially virialized structures, with the CHM passing by rather than being accreted. This dichotomy points to two distinct regimes of secondary bias, a `cold' regime and a `hot' regime, in which tidal and inertial forces act as the main drivers, respectively, with the dominant mechanism migrating from the former to the latter as haloes assemble into massive structures. At fixed large-scale environment, $f_{\rm un}$ further indicates the presence of nearby neighbours and the competitive accretion. Our results highlight the role of unbound matter as a mediator of environmental effects on haloes, and reveal the physical mechanisms that shape the CHM pattern through which these effects are mediated.

paper.title: Black holes in Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity
paper.abstract: We investigate vacuum black-hole solutions in metric-affine Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity (MG-I), where $R$ is the affine Ricci scalar and $T$ is a quadratic torsion invariant, not the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. For the polynomial model $F(R,T)=αR+βT+γT^3$, with $α\neq0$, we first vary the metric and all components of the independent affine connection, and only then specialize to metric-compatible geometry with totally antisymmetric torsion. Nonzero axial torsion admits an exceptional branch $α+β+3γT_*^2=0$, on which the metric satisfies the Einstein equations with effective cosmological parameter $Λ_*=γT_*^3/α$. We establish a local existence result and construct torsionful Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter representatives that are smooth through a selected future Killing horizon. Within the spherically symmetric axial ansatz, we characterize Ricci-symmetric affine connections by the condition $(fV-U)'=0$ and compare a constant-$W=fV-U$ family with a constant-$U$ family. Although these connections share the same metric and torsion scalar, their affine curvature invariants generally differ. Independent coordinate-level curvature contractions and component tests of the unrestricted metric and connection variations corroborate the identities used in the construction; these checks complement the analytic variational derivation. Finally, we identify null directions of the restricted axial quadratic form and distinguish this degeneracy from a complete metric-affine stability analysis. Our conclusions are local and do not establish global extendibility, physical inequivalence of all torsion profiles, or dynamical stability.

paper.title: Relativistic precession around rotating neutron stars. I. Slow rotation: Hartle--Thorne spacetimes, particle orbits and the QPOs of atoll and Z sources
paper.abstract: We study the relativistic precession model (RPM) of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the spacetimes of slowly rotating neutron stars computed from the equation of state (EOS). For four EOSs (WFF1, G3, FSUGarnet and IOPB-I) we solve the Hartle--Thorne equations to second order in the angular velocity and compute the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of the exterior metric without expanding in the spin or the quadrupole. At $1.9\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ the spin-induced quadrupole is 2--4 times that of a black hole with the same spin; it lowers the nodal precession frequency by up to 25 per cent near the innermost stable circular orbit and limits the nodal frequency that any spin can produce. An eccentric, tilted geodesic around a $1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ star spinning at 363~Hz precesses at the epicyclic rates, and the power spectrum of a hot spot on it peaks at the orbital, periastron and nodal precession frequencies. Applied to the atoll sources 4U 1636$-$53 and 4U 1728$-$34, the RPM gives masses of 2.02--$2.15\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and 1.88--$1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. For 4U 1728$-$34 the low-frequency QPO favours stars with large moments of inertia, $I\simeq2.5\times10^{45}$~g\,cm$^{2}$. Without an EOS the QPOs give $M=1.920^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, $j=0.162^{+0.023}_{-0.011}$ and $\bar Q=2.2^{+1.1}_{-0.8}$; a Kerr spacetime with the same nodal frequency would underestimate the moment of inertia by 22 per cent. For the Z sources GX 5$-$1 and GX 340+0 the horizontal-branch oscillations cannot be twice the nodal precession frequency for any of the four EOSs: the fits are driven to spins of 730--745~Hz and to the maximum mass.

paper.title: Scalar charge of neutron stars and accreting black holes in Starobinsky gravity: quasi-universal relations, the trace anomaly and gravitational-wave sensitivity
paper.abstract: The Starobinsky scalaron is sourced by the trace of the stress--energy, so its exterior charge is set by the matter around an object and not by the object's vacuum geometry. We derive a master formula for that charge for any static, spherically symmetric source, evaluate it first for neutron stars, where the interior is known, and then for accreting black holes, where it is not. For a star the pressure subtracts: on the interior metric with the Eardley sensitivity, and the charge is a quasi-universal function of the compactness. Six realistic equations of state confirm the relation but lie above the coefficient calibrated on polytropes; the refit reproduces their mean to 0.007. The trace $ρ-3p$ changes sign in the cores of massive stars, and the charge also tracks the tidal deformability and the moment of inertia to a few parts in 1000 and 100. Solving the Einstein-frame structure equations self-consistently moves a star along this relation and leaves its charge at fixed compactness within 4 per cent of the test-field value. We compare the charge with NICER radii and the GW170817 tidal deformability, and use the published massless dipole constraint from GW230529 to calibrate a Fisher estimate of the sensitivity of a similar binary to a finite scalaron range, projected to the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer; the range is a free parameter, and the laboratory bound on pure $R+αR^2$ is confronted explicitly. A vacuum black hole has q=0; a hole with a disc has $q=\sinh(m_φr_d)/(m_φr_d)$, controlled by the disc's outer edge, which makes it the counterpart in which the same integral is dominated by matter far from the centre; light is blind to the charge at leading order, and the correction beyond it is negligible for any self-consistent disc.

paper.title: Geodesics and a Hubble Relation in Nonstationary Thermodynamic Geometry
paper.abstract: Thermodynamic geometry offers a versatile lens from equilibrium to nonequilibrium, yet typically assumes a stationary metric. Here we study nonstationary thermodynamic geometry, where the metric evolves even at fixed control parameters. The resulting temporal connection generalizes the geodesic equation and redistributes dissipation along optimal control paths. We further establish a thermodynamic Hubble relation that distinguishes relaxation toward equilibrium from geometric expansion or contraction. Brownian examples demonstrate that externally modulated friction can reduce minimum dissipation, while heat exchange with a finite reservoir can induce geometric contraction and Mpemba-type relaxation. Our framework lays a geometric foundation for understanding complex evolving nonequilibrium systems.

paper.title: Disentangling Magnetospheric and Colliding-Wind X-ray and Radio Emission in the Post-Mass-Transfer Magnetic Massive Binary Plaskett's Star
paper.abstract: Plaskett's star is an O+O binary system harboring a kG-order magnetic field associated with the broad-lined secondary. It is the only O-type star believed to host a centrifugally supported magnetosphere. We present orbital- and rotational-phase resolved X-ray and low-frequency radio observations of Plaskett's star. X-ray observations were taken with Chandra using the High Energy Transmission Grating Spectrometer (HETGS), while the radio observations come from uGMRT and VLA. The X-ray light curve shows rotational modulation according to the magnetic component's rotation period, with maximum flux near magnetic minima. We confirm the decline in flux near orbital phase 0.5 where the slow rotator primary is in front of its magnetic companion. We used the $f/i$ ratios of Si XIII and Mg XI from high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy to infer the location of the plasma emitting X-rays. We find no statistically significant variation in line widths or centroid shifts with either orbital or rotational phase; however, given instrumental limitations, this non-detection may partly reflect observational constraints, while still suggesting a complex and extended X-ray emitting plasma distribution. We could not detect the star in the low-frequency radio bands (0.6--1.5 GHz). Re-analysis of existing Very Large Array data reveals an additional detection at 3 GHz, consistent with a nonthermal contribution predicted by magnetospheric models, although no direct signature was obtained. At low frequencies, nonthermal emission from the magnetosphere and the colliding-wind region is likely suppressed by free-free absorption in the winds of one or both components.

paper.title: Discovery of Ultra Fast Outflows in the Narrow Line Seyfert 1 Galaxy Mrk 110 with XMM-Newton and NuSTAR
paper.abstract: We present an X-ray analysis of XMM-Newton and NuSTAR spectra of the Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxy Mrk 110. Our analysis reveals the intriguing presence of a multi-component ultra fast outflow (UFO) both in the grating spectrum and the NuSTAR data. The moderate UFO significance (3-4$σ$), in the grating and CCD data indicates a shallow absorber, consistently with the absence of previous such claims in this source. The two components (UFO1 and UFO2) in the grating spectrum show a fairly wide range of velocities (0.05-0.06c), as their respective ionization state (Log U = -1.43 and -1.82), however they share the same column density (Log N$_H$ $\sim$ 19.7). In the NuSTAR spectrum, we found a much faster wind component with a velocity of $\sim$ 0.21c (UFO3). We show that, in an energy-driven wind scenario, UFO3 might carry enough energy to produce significant feedback on its host galaxy. Considering its known radio properties, Mrk 110 is therefore another Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 with stratified ultra-fast outflows co-existent with a pc-scale jet/outflow radio structure.

paper.title: Comparative Analysis of Influences of Magnetic Field Inputs on Simulating the 2017 September 10 Solar Energetic Particle Event
paper.abstract: Physics-based solar energetic particle (SEP) models simulate the ambient solar wind, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and SEPs using photospheric magnetic field maps as the inner boundary condition. In this study, we select the 2017 September 10 SEP event, which produced the first ground level enhancement observed on the surfaces of both Earth and Mars, to examine how these inputs influence the modeled results. We use the SOlar wind with FIeld lines and Energetic particles (SOFIE) model suite, driven independently by the GONG and ADAPT-GONG magnetic field maps, to simulate the solar wind, CME, and SEPs from the low corona to beyond Mars' orbit. The two maps yield different open flux regions and hence different solar wind conditions, both globally comparable to in situ observations at Earth, STA, and Mars, with the GONG-driven results performing slightly better. We find that in the ADAPT-GONG-driven run, a more energetic CME flux rope propagates into a slower, wider stream, producing broader CME expansion and a more extended shock, which reaches both planets within ~4 hours of the observed arrival, while the GONG-driven run misses both arrivals. Both simulations reproduce the observed SEP fluxes at Earth within a factor of ~3, while the ADAPT-GONG-driven results compare better with observations at Mars, which connects magnetically to the shock flank. Therefore, for this event, the relative performance of the two simulations depends on the observer and observable, with SEP fluxes shaped by CME propagation through the ambient solar wind and by magnetic connectivity to the evolving shock.

paper.title: Kepler as an accidental heliospheric imager: Thomson-scattered solar-wind structure in four years of background photometry
paper.abstract: Kepler recorded several thousand dedicated sky-background pixels per detector output every 29.4 min from 2009 May to 2013 May while staring at a fixed 12-degree field at ecliptic latitude +65 degrees. From this archive we isolate a large-scale layer that measures brightness variations relative to an 8-day running median. This layer contains fluctuations of 0.02-0.1 electrons per second per pixel (about 1e-17 of the mean solar surface brightness) that sweep across the field in a day or less. Four lines of evidence show that these are sunlight Thomson-scattered by solar-wind electrons. (1) The sweeps propagate away from the Sun (84 percent within 45 degrees of the anti-solar direction; 25 percent expected by chance), and their direction follows the Sun through each quarter and across all 16 spacecraft rolls. (2) The field brightness correlates with the near-Earth (OMNI) proton density within a day of zero lag (r = 0.19, p < 1/150), but not with the energetic-proton flux. (3) Time-elongation maps show fronts moving outward at a median 15 degrees per day, as forward models of radially moving density structures predict. (4) The amplitude is about one third of a parameter-free Thomson-scattering prediction and varies by a factor of about 3 over the year, as predicted. Half of the scattered light comes from within 0.4-0.7 AU of the spacecraft. Fronts are strongest in slow wind. Kepler's background pixels thus provide a four-year, high-cadence, out-of-ecliptic record of solar-wind structure near 1 AU. Standard Kepler processing removes these signals, changing stellar light curves by less than about 1 ppm.

paper.title: Dymnikova black string
paper.abstract: We obtain a new static black string solution of Einstein's equations with a negative cosmological constant sourced by a Dymnikova-type anisotropic matter distribution. At large radial distances, the geometry approaches the Lemos black string, while the behavior near the central region is characterized by an effective curvature parameter. We examine the weak and strong energy conditions, the horizon structure, and the curvature invariants. The Ricci and Kretschmann scalars remain finite at the origin. We also investigate the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, with particular attention to the dependence of the thermodynamic behavior on the Dymnikova scale.

paper.abstract: The indirect evidence for magnetic fields in the intergalactic medium motivates the study of their possible primordial origin, including generation during inflation. One mechanism for inflationary magnetogenesis involves a pseudoscalar inflaton coupled to a gauge field through the interaction $g_{φγ}φF_{μν}\tilde{F}^{μν}$. In this work, we study the viability of this mechanism in the context of low scale inflation, particularly on inflationary energy scales near the electroweak (EW) scale. We find that the post inflationary amplification of the gauge fields can produce astrophysically relevant magnetic fields for $g_{φγ}\ge 360~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$ in the absence of Schwinger backreaction for an inflationary scale around the EW scale. We then include the backreaction of the charged current generated through the Schwinger mechanism. We find that the induced current suppresses the gauge field amplification and leads to a saturation of the gauge field energy density at a value of order $m_e^4$, where $m_e$ is the electron mass. Assuming this saturation level, we find that magnetic fields above the lower bound inferred from the non detection of secondary GeV photons from blazars can be obtained when reheating occurs at temperatures below $\sim 0.3$ GeV. For an inflationary energy scale of $100~{\rm GeV}$, achieving this saturation until a reheating temperature, $T\le 0.3~{\rm GeV}$, requires a coupling strength $g_{φγ}\ge 20000~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$. We obtain a present-day magnetic field strength of $B_0 \sim 2\times10^{-13}$ G with a coherence length of $L_{0}\sim 5\times10^{-3}$ kpc for the reheating temperature of $100$ MeV.

paper.title: The PHAROS Spectral Library: Data Processing, Spectral Reconstruction, and Uncertainty Propagation
paper.abstract: We document the data reduction, reconstruction choices, and available uncertainty propagation underlying fifteen PHAROS stellar spectral energy distributions from 0.5 to 5000 nm. A catalogue timeline and a practical FITS guide introduce the available products, their column and extension conventions, and examples of reading, integration, and uncertainty display. Shared methods are presented once, including flux geometry, support-aware integration, X-ray likelihoods, the 2025 X/EUV luminosity relation, intrinsic Ly$α$ inference, airglow treatment, spectral junctions, and covariance-aware resampling. Target sections record the adopted observations and alternatives, including spatially separated binary components, unresolved system-level EUV measurements, direct EUVE constraints, optical stellar-twin transfer, and literature-anchored cases where new spectral inference is unsupported. The distinction between native measurement errors, conditional model intervals, empirical predictive scatter, and physical-method sensitivity is maintained. Signed measurements and nonnegative irradiation products are distinguished. Each target section concludes with the final nominal spectrum and its available uncertainty bounds on common axes. This library provides the detailed provenance and interpretation needed to accompany the catalogue paper and its machine-readable products.

paper.title: Multi-throat generalized Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with asymptotic string-cloud behavior
paper.abstract: We study an ultrastatic, spherically symmetric family of traversable wormholes obtained by locally deforming a generalized Ellis--Bronnikov areal-radius profile in a spacetime with an asymptotic angular deficit. Depending on the deformation parameters, the same analytic family contains one, two, three, or four throats. The corresponding bifurcation curves are obtained in dimensionless form, and the resulting geometries are regular and asymptotically conical. We also reconstruct a source in General Relativity using a canonical scalar, a shift-symmetric phantom scalar, and a magnetic nonlinear electromagnetic field coupled to the canonical scalar. In the reference multi-throat geometry, the coupling removes a branch obstruction of an uncoupled single-valued nonlinear electrodynamics (NED); the same obstruction occurs whenever equal values of the magnetic invariant require different values of $\mathcal G_F$. For $\mathcal G(F)=F+λ\sqrt F$, the NED sector carries the leading asymptotic stress, which scales as $r^{-2}$ and approaches the string-cloud equation of state. The total stress tensor satisfies pointwise energy conditions in finite belly-centered regions of representative two- and four-throat solutions, while the throats violate the radial null energy condition (NEC) and the violation extends into integrable asymptotic tails. The Nandi--Zhang--Kumar covariant volume integral of $ρ+p_r$ is quadratic in the deformation amplitude; its zero is distinct from the bifurcation curves. Away from saddle-node boundaries, each throat supports a radially unstable background-metric light ring, and each intermediate belly supports a radially stable one, with an internally trapped null family in the double-throat case. These results place the topology, source reconstruction, integrated NEC content, and background-metric circular-orbit structure in a common parameter-space description.

paper.title: Polarization of Fast Radio Bursts due to Propagation in Magnetized Plasma
paper.abstract: Polarization measurements of radio transients, particularly their frequency dependence, shed light on the magnetic environments of these sources. We extend the analytical solution of radiative transfer of the polarization properties of such transients to both a cold magnetized plasmas beyond the high-frequency approximation and a relativistic plasma with synchrotron emission. The Faraday mixing coefficients are enhanced makes Stokes parameters $Q$, $U$, and $V$ to exhibit a more rapid and complex frequency-dependent evolution. A relativistic plasma medium can also generate both Faraday roataion and conversion with a smaller magnetic field. The relativistic plasma is investigated as a persistent radio source (PRS) associated with FRB, and it is found that, although the observed PRS luminosity can be accounted for, an FRB can propagate out only under certain special parameter conditions. We apply the model to fit the polarization profile of GPM J1839$-$10 and revisit some FRBs. All sources with Faraday conversion require that the environment's magnetic field not exceed 100~G. The magnetic field of FRB 20180301A and GPM J1839$-$10 are almost perpendicular to the light of sight for at least some times.

paper.title: Stripped White Dwarfs as Spectroscopic Clocks: Abundance Transitions in Partial Tidal Disruptions
paper.abstract: We investigate partial tidal disruptions of He and CO white dwarfs (WDs) by a $10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We construct realistic WD structures and abundance profiles with MESA and map them into FLASH to follow the remnant response and the time-dependent composition of the fallback debris in single pericentre passages on tightly bound orbits ($e=0.9$). The element-specific fallback rates exhibit pre-peak compositional transitions that trace the WD's stratified layers. In the grazing encounter ($β=0.55$), hydrogen dominates the earliest returning debris, followed by helium, showing a H$\rightarrow$He transition. Deeper encounters ($β=0.7$ and $0.8$) penetrate the CO core and produce a He$\rightarrow$C transition, that occurs earlier relative to peak fallback and is stronger in the deeper encounter. These signatures provide a potential spectroscopic diagnostic for identifying CO-WD tidal disruption events (TDEs). We then develop a semi-analytic model for repeated tidal stripping and predict passage-to-passage compositional evolution, in which the stripped material becomes progressively enriched in heavier elements as deeper layers are exposed, leading to stronger and earlier abundance transitions in later flares. We find that WDs can survive several dozen ($\sim 30$-$80$) passages, depending on their initial mass and compactness. Our results link time-dependent abundance signatures to repeating WD disruptions and provide testable observable predictions for identifying IMBH-powered transients.
